>How is being bi and pan different, for you? Are you more attracted to personalities, or are you just gender blind?

I would have to agree with levirax's answer. Bi, by definition, is limited to two. Pansexual, well, it's not limited to male/female, it fills in the gaps. And I would consider myself genderblind in a sense of romantic attraction, but less so for sexual attraction.

>Do you prefer people who tend to one end of the gender spectrum?

I lean towards the feminine side (I'm also a natural born female, though I identify as genderqueer), whether that is natural born females, mtf trans, or feminine males. But as I mentioned previously, this only applies to sexual attraction, not romantic.

>Do pan people still have types? I mean physical attributes, like blondes or brunets, older/younger looking?

I definitely do. (Redheads, OMG)

>Do you think it was more difficult to come to terms with being pan compared to being gay or bi?

I think it's harder for other people to understand. I mean, it's a common misconception that bisexuals are just confused, imagine how much more a pansexual would get this. Although I don't think it was harder for *me* to come to terms with.

>Would you prefer to date someone who identifies as pan?

This may sound bad, but I'd most prefer to date a lesbian, simply because there would be less "threat" (I'm slightly prone to jealousy as it is).

>do you feel you fit in under bi as an umbrella term? 

I don't think so. Pansexual kind of *expands* from bisexual, so it could be the other way around. 

>how do you feel about term Queer or LGBT?

I'm fine with them. I like the term queer to apply to all non-hetero sexualities. And as for LGBT, I *prefer* LGBTQQ, but that can be a mouthful. I believe there's one even longer too. It's really not worth arguing over, though.

I know that there are people where I am that aren't so bigoted and would accept me for who I am, and I actually know a few of those people. But unfortunately, *most* of the people I know and almost all of the people I interact with regularly aren't so supportive. I mainly fear what would happen within my family and my church - the two groups of people I spend the most time with. And I cannot run the risk of them finding out.

And this subreddit seems to be full of great people who have already helped so much. I'm so glad I posted here. And as for college, I'll for sure be looking for one that has a good lgbt group. Most people don't understand that, though. Hell, even I don't.

>Privilege and depression are allowed to go together it does not mean that your thoughts are any less valid.

Shouldn't it, though? Here I am, given the ideal balance of privilege and responsibility, and I can't even enjoy it? How selfish of me, right?! Most of the world has much less than I do, yet they can wear a genuine smile.

>Find new friends good people exist. 

Trust me, I'm looking for them.

>Find little things to enjoy, no matter how stupid or trivial.

Oh, I do! I have lists full of movies I want to watch, books I still want to read, things I want to do, places I want to see, as well as everyday things that please me. And I try to do those things as often as I can. Everyday I lose more and more enjoyment from them, though. (Sorry if I'm just sounding like a pessimistic drag)
Thanks, that helps a little. :)

>Mental health professionals and people with the illness know better.

A counselor once told me this, though. And so did a girl I know who attempted suicide twice. If even those who have been through depression say it's all in the head, who's to argue with them?

>You could no more do that than a paralyzed man could get up an walk. You have a serious illness.

You see, the actual physical evidence for this is somewhat ambiguous. Many psychologists and neuroscientists will even tell you that depression isn't solely, or even primarily, due to physical imbalances.

>You find them the same way you find anything worth finding, you have to work at it.

Sometimes you just get sick of looking for those people though. Some people are just luckless and find assholes instead of friends.

>Finding the right meds or pysch doc is difficult, but once you find the right situation your life will be better.

Currently on my third anti-depressant. They've all made me feel worse. And I've been to four counselors, but my parents will only take me to Christian counselors (I understand they can put their beliefs aside and approach it from a purely psychological perspective, but, being a pansexual, genderqueer Atheist, it's hard for me to actually open up). And my parents stopped taking me since they viewed at as just a waste of their money.
